doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Coltrane's Expressions and leaving pre-med
summary: Coltrane's Expressions was his aha moment; he had already dropped pre-med and his father told him to be the best at whatever he does.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Was there a particular recording that – you’ve indicated that your training was mostly in European classical theory etcetera. Was there a particular jazz recording that you would consider like an AHA! moment?
Oh yeah. It was Coltrane, it was the album – what was it called – “Expressions.”
That’s a heck of a place to start.
Yeah, that was, I mean I had already stopped, I had already dropped out of pre-med, and told my parents I was going to be a musician.
They said they knew it all the time but they had to let me figure it out.
Because my father told me, he said, “You know it doesn’t matter that much what you do. What matters is whatever it is make sure you’re the best at it.”
